commitResults.messageBody:
The task manager lacks a package structure and uses inconsistent naming,
boxed booleans, and undocumented public APIs. These issues make the code
harder to read and inconsistent with the project coding standard.

Move the classes into the ernest package and apply consistent naming,
encapsulation, formatting, and Javadocs. Use primitive boolean state with
boolean-style accessors to make task completion explicit.

Git changes need a consistent format for readable history and safe
collaboration.

Add the project Git skill and mandate imperative subjects, wrapped
WHAT/WHY bodies, and meaningful kebab-case branch names in AGENTS.md.

Java code needs a shared style guide to keep the student project
consistent and readable.

Add the project Java skill and mandate its package, naming, formatting,
encapsulation, and Javadoc rules in AGENTS.md.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tasks: Add support for ToDo, Deadline and Event tasks
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce typed task classes and a TaskList to create, display, mark, and unmark tasks through Ernest's command loop. Parse deadline and event details from /by, /from, and /to fields.

Add a reusable Java 25 runner that executes isolated Ernest CLI sessions, compares complete console output, prints transcripts, and stops on the first failure.\n\nRecord representative todo, deadline, event, marking, exit, and invalid-command cases in the UI test plan, and require agents to review the plan and invoke the skill after code updates.

Keep addTask focused on capacity checks, list updates, and user output. Move deadline, event, and to-do parsing into dedicated helpers so each method has a single level of abstraction and marker positions are calculated once. This makes the command parser easier to read and maintain without changing its observable behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Derive Task Status From Completion State
commitResults.messageBody: Remove the duplicated status field from Task and derive the display marker directly from isDone. A single source of truth prevents the stored status and completion flag from drifting out of sync, while preserving the existing task output for incomplete and completed tasks.

Use a shared task lookup helper and guard clauses in markTask and unmarkTask. Invalid task numbers and already-set states now exit immediately, leaving the successful state transition unindented and reducing duplicated validation flow without changing console behavior.

Add reader-facing Javadocs for the task subtype classes, TaskList, and the TaskList constructor and fields. Document the private parsing helpers as well because their command formats and lookup behavior are not fully obvious. This records the purpose and contract of the existing code without changing runtime behavior.

Name the supported command prefixes and task detail markers, then use their lengths instead of unexplained substring offsets. This makes the parser easier to read and maintain while preserving the existing task descriptions, dates, time ranges, and console output for supported commands.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Java Naming For Event Durations
commitResults.messageBody: Rename Event's duration_start and duration_end fields and constructor parameters to durationStart and durationEnd. The new names follow Java camelCase conventions and make the event model consistent with the rest of the code, without changing task formatting or behavior.

Make Deadline's due date and Event's time-range fields private and final. These values are set only during construction, so preventing subclass and external mutation protects each task's invariants while preserving the existing string representation and command-line behavior.

Make the no-argument Task constructor delegate to the description constructor so the shared incomplete-state initialization has one implementation. Keep taskName mutable because future task-editing behavior may need to update it; this refactoring only removes duplicated setup and preserves the existing constructors and output.

Rename the private Deadline field and constructor parameter from by to dueDate. The command syntax still uses by, but the model field now names the concept it stores, making the code easier to understand without changing the external task representation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate Command Processing From Input Loop
commitResults.messageBody: Keep runChat focused on reading input and controlling the chat lifecycle by moving command normalization, dispatch, and response output into processCommand. The boolean result preserves the existing exit behavior for bye while keeping command-specific logic at one abstraction level.

Guard task creation against missing or misordered deadline and event markers before substring parsing. Without these checks, malformed commands pass invalid indexes to substring and terminate the chatbot with an exception. Report the existing invalid-command message instead and cover both cases in the exact UI test plan.

Bring the code-quality refactorings and malformed-command handling onto master from the branch rooted at 6b19612. Preserve the branch history so the iterative changes remain independently reviewable while master receives the verified final state.

commitResults.messageTitle: Improve command validation and UI coverage
commitResults.messageBody: Validate command words and task details before parsing so malformed user input receives specific messages without substring errors. Handle case-insensitive task commands, whitespace, invalid task numbers, and malformed markers while preserving task descriptions. Expand the exact UI test plan and README documentation to record the new behavior and development workflow.

Encapsulate task storage behind instance methods and validate
deletion arguments so invalid commands do not terminate Ernest.

Synchronize exact UI output expectations and add deletion coverage
for removal, renumbering, and invalid task numbers.

commitResults.messageTitle: test: Resolve merged UI test plan
commitResults.messageBody:
Keep deletion and clear-list scenarios as separate complete cases.

Align persistence output expectations with the merged application.

Ernest handles both command parsing and command execution, which
mixes different abstraction levels.

Move trimming, normalization, and tokenization into a dedicated
Parser class. Return a ParsedCommand value so execution can retain
the user's original casing for task details while dispatching on
normalized command words.

Name command literals as constants and update dispatch formatting to
match the project Java style.

Ernest owns scanner management and user-facing output alongside
command coordination. This mixes interface details with application
flow.

Move console input, standard messages, and display formatting into a
Ui class. Keep command dispatch in Ernest and pass the Ui explicitly
so this increment does not alter task or storage APIs.

Manage the scanner through AutoCloseable to preserve its existing
lifecycle while keeping resource ownership inside Ui.

Ernest passes TaskList and Ui through static helper methods even
though they represent the state and interface of one application run.

Store both components as final fields and make the command loop
instance behavior. Let main construct Ernest and invoke run so the
entry point only starts the application.

Close Ui in a finally block so resource cleanup remains guaranteed.

Command-processing methods return booleans even though they perform
actions, making their return meaning difficult to infer at call sites.

Parse each command once in the chat loop and use isExitCommand as the
only boolean predicate. Make runChat and handleCommand return void so
their action-oriented names match their contracts.

Keep farewell output in the chat loop to preserve the distinction
between an explicit exit and end of input.

The task-capacity check sits inside the exception-handling block used
for malformed records, even though reaching the capacity is normal
control flow.

Move that check before record parsing so the catch block handles only
invalid record data. Align switch labels with project Java style for
consistent readability.

TaskList prints its contents directly, coupling task storage to
console presentation and leaving Ernest unable to coordinate the
interaction.

Expose an unmodifiable task snapshot and let Ui render the numbered
list. Have Ernest pass the snapshot between these components so each
class retains one clear responsibility.

TaskList printed command feedback after clearing its data, coupling a
domain operation to console presentation.

Keep clearTasks focused on mutation and persistence. Let Ernest request
the confirmation from Ui after the operation returns, preserving the
existing output order.

TaskList prints successful deletion details and the remaining capacity,
coupling a list mutation to console presentation.

Return the deleted task from deleteTask and expose the list counts
needed by Ui. Let Ernest request the success message only after a
deletion succeeds, preserving validation and save-warning behavior.

TaskList prints successful mark and unmark confirmations, coupling task
state changes to console presentation.

Return the affected task number when each operation succeeds. Let Ernest
request the corresponding Ui message while preserving validation and
save-warning behavior.

TaskList prints successful addition details and list capacity, coupling
task creation to console presentation.

Return the created task when addTask succeeds. Let Ernest request the Ui
message with the updated counts while preserving validation and
save-warning behavior.

TaskList parses raw numbered commands and prints syntax errors, mixing
command interpretation and user interaction with list operations.

Represent valid, missing, and nonnumeric arguments explicitly in Parser.
Let Ernest route parsing outcomes to Ui and pass only parsed integers to
TaskList, preserving command output.

TaskList returns null and prints semantic errors for numbered
operations, leaving callers unable to distinguish failure reasons.

Return Optional for deletion and dedicated mark and unmark statuses.
Let Ernest map each outcome to Ui so TaskList remains focused on state
changes and no numbered operation depends on null.

TaskList validates raw task commands and constructs task subtypes,
mixing command interpretation with list management.

Return explicit parsing outcomes and constructed tasks from Parser.
Let Ui render parsing failures while TaskList handles only capacity,
mutation, and persistence.

TaskList writes directly to the console when persistence fails, which
mixes list management with user interaction.

Return each operation's domain outcome together with its save status.
Let Ernest coordinate the warning through Ui, and extend the UI test to
cover every mutation path.

Storage prints loading warnings directly, mixing persistence with user
interaction.

Return loaded tasks with an explicit status. Let Ernest construct
TaskList from those tasks and ask Ui to render any warning. Add coverage
for invalid saved-data headers.

TaskList still triggers persistence, and Storage is tied to one static
file path. This keeps list management coupled to file handling.

Give Ernest an instance-configured Storage and save only after
successful TaskList mutations. Keep TaskList focused on in-memory list
operations and make the data path explicit at startup.

Ernest handles every command directly in one switch, leaving no common
execution contract for command subclasses.

Add an abstract Command type and extract ListCommand and HelpCommand.
Route these read-only cases through one dependency-aware execution
method as a low-risk foundation for later command extraction.

Exit, invalid, and clear behavior still lives in Ernest even though a
shared command abstraction exists.

Move those behaviors into Command subclasses, use isExit for loop
termination, and centralize command-side persistence warnings.

Ernest still executes add, delete, mark, and unmark behavior after
parsing each command.

Move those operations, their feedback, and successful-save handling
into dedicated Command subclasses. Leave argument parsing in Ernest for
the next focused increment.

Ernest still interprets parsed command data and selects concrete command
classes, so its main loop retains command-specific branching.

Return executable Command objects from Parser, including validation-error
commands. Reduce Ernest to reading, executing, checking for exit, and
showing the divider.

All classes share the root package, which obscures architectural
boundaries and lets parser and storage status types leak into the UI.

Group classes by responsibility under command, parser, storage, task,
UI, and exception packages. Represent parsing failures with
ErnestException and let Ernest coordinate storage load warnings to keep
dependencies directed.

The UI plan omits parser validation, storage failure, capacity, and CSV
escaping branches, leaving visible regressions undetected.

Add exact-output cases for invalid fixed commands, marker validation,
CSV round-tripping, load failure, and capacity handling. Extend the test
runner with a data-file-directory fixture so load failures can be
reproduced reliably.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support dates and optional times in tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline and event scheduling stores unvalidated text, which prevents
consistent date and time handling.

Parse task dates into typed values, allow optional times in HHmm or
HH:mm form, and persist ISO values. This rejects invalid input and
lets saved tasks round-trip reliably.

Update command help and UI coverage for date-only, date-time, and
invalid input.

Users need a quick way to locate tasks without scanning the full list.

Add case-insensitive substring matching for find, including phrases.

Document find and delete in help and cover the behavior with UI tests.

Add missing Javadocs to command overrides, task accessors, display
methods, and UI resource cleanup. Complete the storage parameter
documentation as part of the repository-wide audit.

This keeps the source API consistent and easier for users to follow
without changing application behavior.

Replace the placeholder guide with concise setup and command guidance. Document every supported command, input format, and persistence behavior so users can operate Ernest without consulting source code.

Events accept end values that occur before their start, producing
invalid ranges in commands and saved data.

Compare required dates and optional times before constructing events.
Reject reversed ranges while allowing equal endpoints and same-date
mixed precision.

Cover both command and storage paths with UI tests.
